title: CWP/1871/2008 of KIRPAL SINGH AND ORS. Vs STATE OF PUNJAB AND ORS.
text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF PUNJAB & HARYANA AT CHANDIGARH 1114 CWP-1871-2008 (O&M) Date of decision: 16.05.2025 Kirpal Singh and others ....Petitioners Versus State of Punjab and others ....Respondents CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMAN CHAUDHARY Present : None for the petitioners. Mr. Manipal Singh Atwal, DAG, Punjab. AMAN CHAUDHARY, J. (ORAL)

1. Prayer made in the present petition for directing the respondents to grant Dearness Allowance to the petitioners as is apparent from para 2 of the writ petition and quashing of order dated 13.09.2007 wherein it has been rejected that in absence of statutory right and the scheme having been repealed w.e.f. 01.06.2003, the claim cannot be accepted.

2. The petitioners working in the Punjab Privately Managed Recognised Aided Schools and retired on attaining the age of superannuation in view of the Punjab Privately Managed Recognised Aided Schools Retirement Benefits Scheme, 1992, which made effective w.e.f. 05.02.1987, those in service on or after the said date were to opt for the same and the petitioners as such exercise their option and adopted the Scheme.

3. Reference has been made to the judgments rendered by the Division Bench in Samdhershi Kumar Bedi and others vs. State of Punjab and another, CWP-11553-2004, decided on 27.09.2005 and Sukhwant Singh and others vs. State of Punjab and others, CWP-6090-2007, decided on 03.05.2007, wherein this issue has been decided, against which no SLP was filed, relevant whereof reads thus:- “In view of the above, we allow these writ petitions. The letter dated 16.07.2003 (Annexure P9) is hereby quashed. All the petitioners who fall within the erstwhile 1992 scheme i.e. they were in service on 05.02.87 and had opted for the pension scheme are held entitled to the grant of pension under the aforesaid Scheme. Let the pensionary benefits be released to the petitioners and all the other similarly situated employees of the aided schools irrespective of whether they have retired before or after 31.05.2003. Let the benefits be released within a period of two months from today.”

4. Relevant para of Sukhwant Singh (supra) read as under:- “In view of the above, we dispose of the writ petitions with a direction to the respondents to release pension of the petitioners at par with their counter parts in the Government and grant them the benefit of dearness pay at par with their counter parts in the Government. The dearness allowance instalments are also required to be at par with the Government employees. We also direct that no recovery from the petitioners should be effect as per the directions issued by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Sahib Ram vs. State of Haryana, 1995(1) SCT 668. The needful shall be done by the respondents within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.”

5. In view of the above, learned State counsel, on instructions, states that the respondents shall consider and decide the claim of the petitioners, taking note of the aforesaid judgments, expeditiously, in accordance with law, uninfluenced by the order impugned in the present case, which this Court has no reason to believe the authorities would not address in a just, fair and reasonable manner.

6. The matter stands disposed of accordingly and if the petitioners are found entitled, grant the benefit forthwith. Needless to say, if the orders are adverse to their interest, the same may be passed after granting opportunity of hearing to them and shall contain reasons, whereupon they shall be free to seek legal redress thereupon. (AMAN CHAUDHARY) JUDGE 16.05.2025 ashok
